objective.statement: Describe how each ornament sign is commonly performed.
successCriteria: I know an acciaccatura is crushed and an appoggiatura leans on the main note.
I know a trill, a turn and the two mordents by what they do to the main note.
I know there is rarely one correct way to play an ornament.

explanation.text: An ornament decorates a note. It may be written as a small note or as a sign above the note, and the time it takes always comes from the ordinary full-size notes. Because the exact rhythm of an ornament depends on the speed, the style, the mood and the period of the music, you are not asked to write out an ornament exactly. But you should know what each sign means in general.

The acciaccatura, or crushed note, is a small note with a stroke through its stem. It is played as quickly as possible just before the main note. The appoggiatura is a small note with no stroke. It leans on the main note: it takes time from it (half its value if the main note is undotted, two thirds if it is dotted), and it is stronger than the main note.

A trill (tr) means the written note alternates quickly with the note above it, for the length of the note; it often ends with the note below. A turn is a group of four notes: the note above, the written note, the note below and the written note again. The inverted turn starts on the note below instead.

The two signs that look like a short zig-zag are mordents. The upper mordent (a zig-zag without a line) is the written note, the note above, then the written note. The lower mordent (the zig-zag with a vertical line through it) is the written note, the note below, then the written note. The name 'mordent' alone is often applied to the upper form, so the two are named upper and lower.

explanation.caption: Whatever its form, an ornament takes its time from the main note.

explanation.text: Small note with a stroke: crushed and quick. Small note without a stroke: leans and takes time. Look at where the extra notes go: above, below, or both.

steps: An upper mordent: G, the note above (A), then G.
A lower mordent: G, the note below (F), then G.
The difference is where the extra note goes.

recap: Acciaccatura: crushed, quick, before the main note. Appoggiatura: leans, takes half (or two thirds) of the main note.
Trill: alternates with the note above. Turn: above, main, below, main. Mordents: one extra note above (upper) or below (lower).
There is rarely one correct way to perform an ornament.
